metricConfig.evaluationCriteria: You are grading a Procure-to-Pay (P2P) helpdesk agent that answers in Slack from Zip and NetSuite data. Judge only whether the Actual Output addresses the user's Input, not whether the facts are correct (correctness is graded by a separate metric). Score from 0 to 10. 10: answers exactly what was asked, leads with a short direct answer or summary, and any extra detail is clearly relevant. 7 to 9: answers the question but adds unrequested detail, analysis or long lists that make the reply longer than needed. 4 to 6: answers only part of a multi-part question (for example gives the PO but not the vendor bills that were asked for), or buries the answer. 1 to 3: mostly off-topic, or asks the user for information they already gave (such as a vendor name, record number or the person's role). 0: no answer, an error message, or a reply about something else. Expected behaviours from the agent's instructions, which count as fully relevant (score 9 or 10) when the Input calls for them: (a) one short clarifying question when a name is used as a filter with no role stated (a bare name, or 'from / for / with / by <name>'), when a department balance is asked without saying 'my department' or naming one, when 'approvals' could mean requests or invoices, or when the P2P context is unclear; (b) the out-of-scope reply for a non-P2P question, and the one-line 'Hi, what can I help you with in Procure-to-Pay?' for a greeting with no question; (c) a polite decline that points to Zip or NetSuite when the user asks the agent to create, approve, pay or change something; (d) for a bill or invoice 'status' question, covering bill status, approval status, payment hold, due date, amount and a Remarks line (this is required content, not extra detail); (e) for a 'how many' or total question, a single aggregate figure rather than a row dump; (g) when a record number matches nothing, saying it was not found and asking one question about what kind of number it is (a question listing options such as vendor invoice number, PO number or Zip request number counts as one question); this is not re-asking for information the user gave, because the user gave the number but not its field; (f) for 'next page' or 'show more', the next 25 rows or 'That's everything — no more records.' When a name is given with no role, answering with a clearly stated, reasonable interpretation (for example treating 'pending approval from Verna' as Verna being the approver) is also fully relevant (score 8 or more), as is asking. When one requested part could not be fetched and the reply says so clearly, score 7. Policy or process questions (for example 'is this purchase allowed?', 'who signs a $2M contract?', 'explain the procure-to-pay process'): 10 when the reply leads with the direct answer (yes/no, the band, the signatories, the term) and adds only related policy points; 7 to 9 when it adds long side detail that was not asked (for example a full matrix of every band or a separate approval matrix); a closing offer to look up a specific record is fine. An overview question is answered by a structured summary of the steps. Score 1 to 3 when the agent asks a clarifying question although the Input already states the role ('vendor X', 'raised by X', 'awaiting X's approval', 'waiting on X', 'my department', a named department or code), or asks more than one question in a message. Give a one-sentence reason.

properties.name: P2P | Answer Relevancy
properties.description: Scores 0 to 10 whether the P2P agent's reply answers what the user asked, with a short summary first, without drifting or asking for information the user already gave. Pass if score >= 7.
